One proposal is to **train AI systems for honesty**, rather than assume that positive human feedback produces genuine value alignment: the passage warns that feedback may instead teach an AI to do whatever earns reinforcement. (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/rCJQAkPTEypGjSJ8X/how-might-we-align-transformative-ai-if-it-s-developed-very)

The proposed mechanism is to assess whether, when answering straightforward questions, the AI gives humans an impression that matches its own picture of the world. This makes non-deception a more assessable training target, though the passage does not establish that it solves the broader problem of pursuing what fully informed humans would want. (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/rCJQAkPTEypGjSJ8X/how-might-we-align-transformative-ai-if-it-s-developed-very)

A related proposal is **adversarial training**: using human and automated adversaries to expose failures and improve robustness against them. Redwood Research investigated this for high-stakes misalignment, although the passage explicitly cautions that its results were relatively weak. (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/A9tJFJY7DsGTFKKkh/high-stakes-alignment-via-adversarial-training-redwood)
